§6.7 Recognising Ambiguous Headings

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

headings-recognising-ambiguous-headings · rule headings structure

✅ Normative

A standalone structural title that organises what follows MUST be rendered as a heading. Run-in labels, repeated item labels, captions and page furniture MUST keep their own roles and MUST NOT be rendered as headings. Font size alone MUST NOT decide whether a line is a heading.

What a line does decides its role; its depth is chosen afterwards. A short bold line can organise a section; a large banner can belong entirely to a form or a table.

Company name over a title    ← its own line, above the heading
Company name alone           ← furniture
Document title               ← heading
Standalone section title     ← heading
Bold label: value or sentence ← inline label
Table 1: ...                 ← caption

Heading depths in the samples below are relative wherever the crop does not show the outline above the heading: the rendering keeps the hierarchy the crop shows, and the absolute level comes from Heading Depth Across Pages§4.5.

Run-in labels

A label followed on the same line by a sentence, value or URL MUST stay inline, with its printed emphasis preserved. A line that wraps onto another line remains the same paragraph. See Run-In Headings§6.8.

✅ Sample — run-in labels 1


Source: Federal Rules of Evidence, Rule 410 (public domain)

“(a) PROHIBITED USES.” stays inline with its sentence; its small capitals are transcribed as capitals. The standalone “Rule 410. Pleas, Plea Discussions, and Related Statements” is a heading. The crop clips item (3), which is elided.

Standalone subheads

A standalone title that organises the paragraphs or bullets below it MUST be a heading, even at body-text size. Weight, colour and underlining support the reading; none decides it alone.

✅ Sample — standalone subheads 1

“Highlights:” and its subordinate “Summary” are headings; each introduces the bullet block below. “Summary” is one level deeper than “Highlights:”. The quotation above is elided.

Expected Markdown · excerpt

…

Highlights:

Summary

  • Revenue growth of 9.0% driven by our market-leading network, strong brands and operational focus
  • Operating profit before exceptional items increased by 26.7% to €4,443 million (2023: €3,507 million) as we continue to execute our transformation programme
  • Structural improvements delivering a world-class operating margin before exceptional items of 13.8% (2023: 11.9%)
  • Free cash flow of €3,556 million, after investing €2,816 million into the business
  • Return on invested capital of 17.3%, as a result of disciplined capital allocation
  • Delivering sustainable value creation for our shareholders

Numbered titles and numbered paragraphs

A printed number or letter MUST stay with the standalone section title it numbers. A number opening a body sentence is a list marker. A number on a line by itself does not turn its paragraph into a section. See Numbered Section Headings§6.5.

In addition, the Contractor shall ensure that all employees and volunteers who use vehicles to transport clients or deliver services have personal automobile insurance and current driver's licenses.

Repeated item labels

Repeated Question, Interrogatory and Request for Production labels MUST stay with their items, even when bold and on their own lines. Each label MUST NOT be made a document heading.

Document titles and company lines

A document title MUST be separated from its logo, company-name line and exhibit label. The surrounding words are transcribed as furniture; only the title takes a heading role. A company name MUST NOT be joined to a title merely because they are stacked.

Principal statement and schedule titles

The principal title of a financial statement or numbered schedule is structural and MUST be a heading. The company line and the units or audit-status line MUST stay separate. This is a specific exception to the caption rule below: a statement or schedule can itself be a document section.

A numbered schedule title remains structural when printed inside a grid. Its text MUST appear once, in its printed table position; it keeps its heading role in the element classes and boxes (see Boxes and Granularity§3.3) and MUST NOT be duplicated as a Markdown heading outside the table. Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3 governs its cell placement.

Table captions and bands

An ordinary table caption, coloured title band, repeated caption stack or column label MUST NOT enter the document outline. A Table N caption remains a caption even when its typography resembles a heading or it appears in a PDF outline. The principal-statement exception above applies only to an actual statement or schedule section.

Captions stay outside the table and title bands inside it, as Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3 requires. The same title MUST NOT be emitted both as a cell and as an outside heading.

Chart titles and text-column titles

A title naming a chart is part of that chart. A standalone title organising a text column or explanatory block below or beside the charts MUST be a heading.

✅ Sample — chart titles and text-column titles 1

Slides and embedded forms

The principal slide title and a real subtitle are structural titles and MUST be headings. Navigation sidebars, tabs, warning banners and form section labels are furniture or form labels and MUST NOT be headings. Titles inside an embedded form screenshot MUST NOT enter the containing slide's outline; their printed text MUST be kept in the embedded content.

“Caldrivane submission schedule” is the slide title and “Supplementary indications for existing brands” its subtitle. “Content” stays in the navigation sidebar. The navigation tabs print no text. Depths assume the file is a deck, where each slide title is top level.

Running headers and decorative marks

Whether a page-top label is a running header is a document decision, made in Recurring Page Furniture§4.6: the same words may have been a section heading where the section began, and repetition at a page boundary does not open it again. From one page alone, a margin label that carries no argument of its own is furniture. A purely decorative arrow before a heading MUST be omitted from the heading text; a printed section number MUST be kept.

✅ Sample — running headers and decorative marks 1

When “Consolidated Financial Statements” repeats at the page top, it is a running header: a band paragraph, not a heading. The repetition is established on the surrounding pages; this crop alone does not establish it. The Markdown shown assumes it does.

Depth comes after role

Heading levels MUST be the document-absolute levels of Heading Depth Across Pages§4.5. When only one page is available, the relative hierarchy the page shows MUST be kept consistent. The first heading on a page MUST NOT be assumed to be the top level, and a level that is common elsewhere MUST NOT be assumed for this page. Whether the deck convention applies is decided once for the file in Document Type§4.4; a level MUST NOT be copied from another document.
